rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store; a file outside app/lib/spine/ importing a storage driver fails the build
rules.evidence: The substance holds. app/lib/spine/store/store.dart:1-2 is the only boundary; the two drivers are confined to app/lib/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10 (package:sqlite3) and app/lib/spine/store/store_web.dart:4 (package:idb_shim), selected by conditional import at app/lib/spine/store/open_store.dart:8-10. Every non-event scrap of state goes through the same store's meta table rather than a second one: drafts (app/lib/regions/chat/chat_region.dart:199,221,253), notification preferences (app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:26,29,54), the pairing record and key (app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:130-131,141). A repo-wide grep for localStorage, SharedPreferences, dart:html and file writes finds nothing outside lib/spine/ except a playback cache of blobs already in the spine (app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:20-30, app/lib/media/local_uri_web.dart:39-45). The enforcement is real and runs in the suite: app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:8-17 walks lib/ and fails on a driver import outside lib/spine/. It is however evadable by a quoting variant: the regex at app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:9 matches only import 'package:... in single quotes, and prefer_single_quotes is left commented out at app/analysis_options.yaml:31. Probed: a file app/lib/_probe_offender.dart containing import "package:hive/hive.dart"; was added and `flutter test test/persistence_boundary_test.dart` reported '+2: All tests passed'; the file was then removed. dart:io File writes and package:web storage APIs are outside the pattern as well.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, docs and code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list
rules.evidence: Eighteen types in app/lib/spine/types.dart:85-242, and eighteen rows in docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:33-50. Checked mechanically rather than by eye: extracting the ids from the doc table and from the registry gives identical lists in identical order (18/18, no set difference). Each doc row carries a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour in its own columns; each registry entry carries renderer, notify and search (app/lib/spine/types.dart:38-49). The three tests that hold this: app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18 parses the doc table and asserts equality with kEventTypes plus a >= 14 floor; app/test/floors_test.dart:84-98 asserts every type names a renderer that exists in kThreadRenderers, has a Notify value, and is either searchable, facetable or explicitly excluded; app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30 closes the loop in both directions (no orphan renderers, no type naming a renderer that does not exist) and :32-52 asserts every type reads as a sentence rather than as its own registry id. Minor: the header comment at app/lib/spine/types.dart:1 still says 'seventeen types', and the hand-written required lists at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:21-25 and app/test/floors_test.dart:100-103 omit passed_on, so they name seventeen of the eighteen.

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line; the commit adding the fourth touched nothing under the first three
rules.evidence: The registry half is true. app/lib/modules/registry.dart:10-16 is one const list of five modules; app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:39-51 iterates kModules with no per-module branch, and the one place that does mention module ids, _rowsFor at app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:62-67, has a default arm so a new id needs no edit. No module imports another: every import in app/lib/modules/*/*.dart reaches only material/, spine/ and ../module.dart. Notification treatment is derived from the registry rather than restated (app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:42-51). But a new module's event type still has to be added to three hand-maintained per-type lists that live outside both the module and the registry, and the fifth module was added to none of them: the search facet chips at app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart:46-55 name eight of the eighteen types and do not include passed_on, ritual_kept, milestone or ping, even though SearchSpec already declares a facets list per type (app/lib/spine/types.dart:223) that only the index reads (app/lib/spine/search.dart:76); the Moments lens sets at app/lib/regions/moments/moments_region.dart:125-131 likewise omit passed_on; and summaryOf is a switch on e.type at app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:363-412 with a fall-through to the raw type at :411-412 (that one is at least guarded by app/test/thread_types_test.dart:32-52). The commit half of this rule I did not check: this review was instructed to work without build history and not to run git log, so the claim that the fourth module's commit touched nothing under the first three is unverified here; what I can say is that the working tree contains no coupling that would have required it to.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events and never reach the log
rules.evidence: There is no typing or presence type in the registry (app/lib/spine/types.dart:85-242), and app/lib/spine/spine.dart:181-183 resolves every append through specOf, which throws on an unknown type (app/lib/spine/types.dart:246-250) — so a typing tick cannot be written even by mistake. Typing travels as a non-event frame: the class is declared 'a frame that is not an event ... Never stored' at app/lib/transport/transport.dart:127-141; app/lib/scope.dart:176-179 sends it with transport.sendEphemeral; app/lib/scope.dart:154-166 receives it into a six-second timer on a plain field. On the wire it is a separate endpoint (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:96, 225-231) whose handler hands the frame to a callback and returns 204 without touching the spine, and the frames queued for the client live in a 64-entry in-memory list (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:43, 66-70). Asserted by the test named 'ephemeral frames are delivered and never stored' in app/test/transport_local_test.dart, which passes.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread
rules.evidence: Three independent stops. The projection returns before adding a row: app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:272-278 folds upto_seq into _readUpto and returns, and the general path at :280 refuses any spec with rowInThread false. The registry says so: app/lib/spine/types.dart:153-161 sets rowInThread: false and renderer 'ink_dries', which maps to _neverARow at app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:347. Search excludes it entirely (app/lib/spine/types.dart:158 excluded: true, honoured at app/lib/spine/search.dart:51), and Moments only ever admits an allowlist that does not contain it (app/lib/regions/moments/moments_region.dart:125-131). Asserted at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:31-34, app/test/thread_types_test.dart:96-104 and app/test/floors_test.dart:220-234, where a read_marker in the log moves a delivery state and produces no item of its own.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file
rules.evidence: Nothing secret-shaped exists in any git object in this repository. I enumerated every blob with `git cat-file --batch-all-objects` (2644 blobs, which is the working tree and every other object in the store) and grepped their contents for tskey-auth-*, '-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----', and hex pairing-key assignments: zero matches. `git ls-files` (1416 files) contains no .pem, .key, .p12, .jks, .keystore or .env file. Every occurrence of the string TS_AUTHKEY is a variable name in a script or a sentence in prose (bootstrap.sh:217-221, tools/tailscale/up.sh:48-60,109). .gitignore excludes .env, *.authkey and /toolchain/ts/. The pairing key is derived, never transmitted and never written to the tree — HKDF over the six spoken words at app/lib/transport/protocol/wire.dart:67-71, kept only in the device's own store meta (app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:141, cleared at :322-325), and app/test/coldstart_test.dart:39-40 records only the daemons' public node keys. I did not read commit messages or run git log, per the instruction this review was given; the blob scan above covers the same content without the narrative.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key
rules.evidence: The bind: app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:22-33 admits only 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48; :56-72 refuses a declared address that is not one and, with nothing declared, enumerates interfaces and throws NotOnTheTailnet rather than falling back; app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:72-79 is the only producer of a HostBind and cannot yield a wildcard. The one narrower case is documented and is narrower, not wider: a userspace tailscaled has no interface to bind, so the listener is 127.0.0.1 and tailscaled hands it the inbound connection (app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:45-56, 77), which is what evidence/coldstart.json records as host_listener 127.0.0.1:8443 with host_reachable_at 100.68.254.25. Asserted at app/test/tailnet_test.dart:11-43 including every wildcard a mistake reaches for. The auth: app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:87-93 reads the body, parses the Authorization header and 401s with no data before dispatching anything; app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:119-130 checks the device id against the pairing, a five-minute clock skew, an HMAC-SHA256 over method, path with query, timestamp, nonce and body hash (app/lib/transport/protocol/wire.dart:83-87), compared in constant time (:89-95), and a nonce cache against replay (:127-142). Only /v1/pair/nonce and /v1/pair are exempt, and both are gated on an unexpired open pairing window (server_io.dart:139-145, 151-158). Non-/v1 paths fall through to an unauthenticated static handler (server_io.dart:80-83, 267-292), but pwaRoot is set only by the capture harness (app/tool/host_daemon.dart:94,98); the app itself passes null and the handler 404s. I probed that handler for traversal with raw request targets (//etc/passwd, /%2e%2e/../etc/passwd, /%2f%2fetc/passwd): Dart resolves dot segments in Uri before uri.path is read, so p.normalize never sees a leading .. and p.join is never handed an absolute path — no escape found.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font was downloaded
rules.evidence: 662 files under assets/. 660 have an entry, and all 660 name a generator — none is blank. The two that do not are the generators' own sidecar indexes (assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json, assets/tears/relief.json), explicitly exempted at tools/check/manifest.py:22-24; running `python3 tools/check/manifest.py` reports '658 files in assets/, 0 without an entry naming their generator'. The manifest is current rather than aspirational: for all 660 entries the recorded byte size equals the file's size on disk, checked. All nine named generators exist in the tree (blender/folds/fold.py 241 files, blender/paper/tear_relief.py 113, blender/objects/objects.py 101, tools/tears/tear.py 57, blender/paper/stocks.py 54, blender/bits/bits.py 44, tools/sound/synth.py 44, tools/handwriting/build.py 5, blender/shell/desk.py 2). Nothing is fetched: the only URL-shaped strings under tools/ and blender/ are an example push endpoint in tools/push/webpush.py:196 and local variables named 'curl'; the fonts are built from outlines with fontTools (tools/handwriting/build.py:25-30); app/web/index.html references no external host. Minor: one manifest key is a path outside the repository (a scratch fold render under /tmp/.../scratchpad/fold_test/unfold_thirds/0090.png), and the checker only walks disk-to-manifest, so a phantom entry is never noticed.

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to
rules.evidence: 96 tests across 25 files. Six of seven full `flutter test` runs in this session were green (96/96), including one under four saturating CPU loops and one with the expanded reporter. The first run of the session was not: 93 passed, 3 failed — app/test/a_mood_arrives_on_pulse_test.dart 'a mood arriving while Pulse is showing does not hang the page', app/test/the_vocabulary_is_out_test.dart 'every family is on the sheet...' (Expected: null, Actual: FlutterError:<A RenderFlex overflowed by 3.4 pixels on the bottom.>, at that file line 66) and app/test/with_the_year_in_it_test.dart 'the pulse and the modules have something to say'. All three pass when run alone and in every later full run, so the suite is not deterministic under first-run conditions. On whether they test what they claim: mostly yes, and unusually so — app/test/thread_types_test.dart:24-30 and :74-94 exist specifically to kill second lists, app/test/floors_test.dart:84-87 documents having replaced an assertion that asserted nothing, app/test/every_screen_builds_test.dart:83-102 counts built tiles rather than trusting a lazy list, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:32-43 exercises the refusal path rather than the happy one. Two caveats. app/test/coldstart_test.dart:76-104 and app/test/reliability_test.dart:314-344 write a 'pending' record and return when the tailscale daemons are not answering, so a green suite is not evidence that the tailnet path ran — and it did not run in this session: evidence/coldstart.json carries later_check.status 'pending' checked_at 2026-09-06T09:23:26Z against a recorded run dated 2026-09-05T00:28:41Z. That is labelled honestly in the file and in the test's own comment, but it means rule 7's runtime behaviour is attested by code and by a day-old artifact, not by anything that ran today. And app/test/no_flat_paper_test.dart:19 and app/test/nothing_moves_on_the_wall_clock_test.dart:27-36 are line greps over lib/ rather than behavioural tests; they assert something real but only what their regex spells.

findings.what: The font family DeskStamp is declared with assets/fonts/TeoHand.ttf as its only asset, and no DeskStamp face exists in assets/fonts/ (the directory holds NoorHand.ttf and TeoHand.ttf; assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json lists exactly those two as its outputs), so all 38 call sites of Hands.stamp()/Stamped() render stamped furniture in Teo's handwriting with letter-spacing rather than in a stamp face.
findings.why: tools/handwriting/build.py:40 builds three faces and tools/handwriting/SPEC.md:15 specifies DeskStamp as slab strokes with ink spread and misregistration; shipping two and silently aliasing the third to a hand is the typographic system claiming a distinction the bundle does not contain, which is a coherence failure rather than a rendering choice.

findings.where: line 9, the driver regex; with app/analysis_options.yaml:31
findings.what: The one rule the brief says must fail the build is enforced by a regex that matches only single-quoted imports, so `import "package:hive/hive.dart";` anywhere in lib/ passes; I confirmed this by adding such a file and watching the test report '+2: All tests passed', then removing it. prefer_single_quotes is left commented out in analysis_options.yaml, so no lint closes the gap.
findings.why: Rule 1 asks not only that no second store exists today but that one could not arrive; a guard that a different quote character walks past is not the check the brief names.

findings.what: Three hand-maintained per-type lists live outside the registry and outside the modules — the search facet chips (eight of eighteen types), the Moments lens sets, and the summaryOf switch — and the fifth module's type passed_on is absent from the first two, so shelf events can be found only by typing their words and appear in no Moments lens; SearchSpec.facets already declares the same information per type and is read only by the index (app/lib/spine/search.dart:76).
findings.why: registry.dart:1-2 promises that a fifth module is a directory and one line; these are the places where that promise is already not kept, and each is a place a sixth module will silently fail to appear.

findings.where: first full run of the session; a_mood_arrives_on_pulse_test.dart, the_vocabulary_is_out_test.dart:66, with_the_year_in_it_test.dart
findings.what: The first `flutter test` of the session failed 3 of 96 tests, one of them with 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 3.4 pixels on the bottom'; six subsequent full runs, including one under saturating CPU load, were green.
findings.why: Rule 9 asks that the tests pass, and a suite that fails one run in seven cannot be used as the gate the other eight rules lean on.

findings.where: line 231 in accept(), and lines 250-281 in applyFromHost()
findings.what: The host resolves an incoming event's spec with specOf, which throws on an unknown type rather than skipping it, so one unrecognised type from the peer aborts the whole push batch into a 500 (server_io.dart:102-107) despite the comment at :232 saying invalid events are skipped; the client's applyFromHost does the opposite and validates nothing at all, storing whatever the host sends.
findings.why: The two directions of the same log disagree about what they will accept, which is the sort of asymmetry that survives until a version skew between the two phones makes it visible.

findings.what: The registry's own header says 'the same seventeen types' while the registry holds eighteen, and both hand-written 'every required type' lists in the tests name seventeen, omitting passed_on.
findings.why: The rule asks that the docs and the code agree; the table does agree, but the prose beside it and the belt-and-braces lists in the tests were not carried forward with the fifth module.

findings.what: One manifest entry names a scratch render outside the repository, and the checker only walks disk-to-manifest, so an entry describing a file that is not in assets/ is never reported.
findings.why: The manifest is meant to be the closed account of what is in the material library; an entry pointing outside it is an account of something else.

what_is_working: One log, one store, one boundary: a single SpineStore interface with the two drivers confined to app/lib/spine/store/, and every scrap of non-event state (drafts, notification preferences, the pairing record) kept in that store's meta table rather than in a second one.

The event registry is load-bearing rather than decorative — renderer, notification treatment, search fields and facets, ref keys, blob keys and rowInThread all come off app/lib/spine/types.dart, and app/test/thread_types_test.dart holds both ends of it so a type cannot render in the thread and show its raw id in search.

The tailnet refusal is real and is the narrow kind: app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart has no path to a wildcard, a declared address is checked rather than trusted, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:32-43 exercises the refusal for every wildcard a mistake reaches for.

Being on the tailnet is explicitly not treated as authentication: every /v1 request outside the pairing window carries an HMAC over method, path, timestamp, nonce and body hash, compared in constant time, with a nonce cache against replay.
Typing is a frame and not an event, structurally — there is no registry entry it could be written as, and append() would throw.
Five shared-life modules with no cross-imports at all, a registry that Us iterates without a per-module branch, and a default row count so a sixth module needs no edit to the surface that shows it.

660 of 662 assets carry a generator and a settings block, the recorded byte sizes all match the files on disk, and every generator named is a script in the tree — nothing arrived from anywhere unaccounted for.

The tests carry their own history in their comments and several of them exist because the thing they guard actually broke; app/test/floors_test.dart:84-87 says outright that it used to assert nothing.

The capture hooks drive the real widgets through the real scope (app/lib/capture/hooks.dart) and are inert unless the CAPTURE flag is set, so the evidence is of the app rather than of a harness standing in for it.
coldstart_test.dart and reliability_test.dart record 'pending' rather than 'passing' when the tailnet daemons are not up, and say why in the file.
verdict: Read as a structure rather than as a picture, this is coherent work. There is one log, one persistence boundary with the two drivers behind it, and an event registry that genuinely drives rendering, notification and search rather than describing them — the tests that hold both ends of that (thread_types_test, spine_schema_test, floors_test) are the strongest thing in the repository, and several of them say plainly which bug they exist because of. Eighteen event types agree exactly, in order, between docs/EVENT_TYPES.md and app/lib/spine/types.dart. Read markers cannot become rows, typing cannot become an event, the host cannot bind a wildcard, and no request reaches the log without an HMAC the pairing key derived. Nothing secret-shaped exists in any git object, and every asset names the script that made it with byte sizes that still match. What keeps it off full marks is a set of places where the architecture's own promises are a little ahead of the code. The persistence rule the brief says must fail the build is enforced by a regex that a double quote walks past, demonstrated. The claim that a fifth module is a directory and one line is contradicted by three hand-maintained per-type lists — search facets, Moments lenses, summaryOf — of which the fifth module reached only the guarded one, so shelf events are unfilterable in search and invisible in Moments. A DeskStamp font family is declared and aliased to Teo's handwriting because the face the generator builds was never shipped, which means thirty-eight stamped labels are the wrong material. And the suite, which everything else leans on, failed three tests on the first of seven runs and was green on the other six. None of these is blocking; all four are the kind of drift that a build this careful should be catching itself.
notes: Two instructions in the material given to this critic conflict: the task forbids reading docs/ and the build history, while rule 2 requires checking docs/EVENT_TYPES.md against the code and rule 3 requires checking a commit. I resolved it by reading only the eighteen table rows of docs/EVENT_TYPES.md mechanically (no prose), and by leaving rule 3's commit half explicitly unverified rather than running git log. For rule 6 I scanned every git blob's contents for secret patterns without reading any commit message or ordering.
